Why do you yawn when someone else yawns?
Even reading or hearing about yawning can set it off.
You might yawn before this video ends.
First, why we yawn at all.
One leading idea: a big yawn pulls in cool air and blood, and helps cool down your brain.
In studies, people with a cold pack on their forehead yawned less.
Okay, but why is it contagious?
You catch yawns more from family and friends than from strangers.
And little kids don't catch yawns at all...
until around age four or five.
Chimpanzees catch yawns from each other.
And dogs can catch yawns from their humans.
Babies already yawn in the womb, at around eleven weeks.
